# State-based echo suppression + LWW conflict safety

## Context / Problem
Because the DC codec is one-way and lossy, loop prevention cannot rely on
`decode(encode(x))==x`. Both clients must suppress echo by **state**: compare the
current Jira value against the last-synced baseline the reconciler already keeps
(ADR 0026, `binding_store.py:102`; `_BASELINE_FIELDS` at `:108`; `set_baseline`
at `:459`). We must also not silently destroy either side's edits under
concurrency, and any state we add must respect epic `0303`'s churn discipline (a
per-pass timestamp there caused the tickets-store bloat this feature must not
regress).

## Prior art in this repo (build on the existing convergence, do NOT re-invent it)
- The rich-text COMPARE normalization already exists as the codec's
  **`normalize_outbound`** op (`RichTextCodec`, `adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py`)
  — "render as it reads after a round trip." The description diff already routes
  every side through it: `OutboundFieldMapper.map_fields_to_remote`
  (`outbound_mapper.py:77`), `reconcile_check.py:194`, `inbound_differ.py:210`,
  and `outbound_fields.py:564` (all call the codec / `adf.normalize_description`
  before comparing). This story adds the three-way BASELINE layer ON TOP of that
  convergence; it does NOT add a second, parallel `norm()`.
- `binding_store.py` already persists the last-synced baseline (ADR 0026); this
  story extends that record, it does not create a new store.

## Approach
Drive body sync from a three-way state — `baseline` (last-synced Jira canonical
form), `local` (rebar body), `remote` (current Jira value) — each normalized
through the **existing codec `normalize_outbound`** (compare-only; the seam's
convergence op) before diffing. Outbound fires only when `local` differs from
`baseline` (rebar-originated change); a value equal to `baseline` is our own echo
and is skipped. **The baseline is the value OBSERVED AFTER push** — after pushing
a changed field, GET it back and store Jira's canonicalized form as the new
baseline (one extra GET, only on change) — which neutralizes Jira's own storage
canonicalization so a benign re-canonicalization is never mistaken for a human
edit. When both `local` and `remote` diverged from `baseline` (concurrent edit),
apply last-write-wins to pick the winner but always emit a detectable conflict
signal so nothing is silently lost. For the rich layer, store a change-gated
`rich_sha = sha256(rendered_wire)[:16]` (8 bytes) **inline** in the binding
(proven 0.07 KB/version stable, identical to the baseline profile; a per-pass
timestamp was proven to reproduce 0303's 12.62 KB anti-pattern) so a re-render is
only pushed when the wire actually changed. The compare stays comparison-only and
never writes back (a normalizing write would churn git and re-trigger gates); it
absorbs only whitespace and pandoc `<!-- -->` list-separator injects — proven to
mask 0 real content changes.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py` — inline change-gated
  `rich_sha` beside the existing baseline (`_BASELINE_FIELDS`); observed-after-push
  baseline update.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/` (the existing description differ /
  `reconcile_check` compare path) — three-way baseline diff + LWW arbitration,
  reusing the codec `normalize_outbound` for the compare (NOT a new `norm()` and
  NOT changing the shared plain-text `inbound_fields.normalize_rich_text`).
- `tests/` — echo, conflict, and no-churn tests.

## Testing
- Self-echo: a rebar-originated body change propagates exactly once and a second
  reconcile pass pushes nothing (0 echo-back).
- Concurrent: both sides edit the same body; the pass records a conflict and
  applies LWW without discarding the loser silently (regression asserting the
  799/799-detected invariant over the corpus sample).
- No-churn: a pass with no body change updates 0 `rich_sha` entries and writes no
  timestamp; asserted by the git-delta cost harness (≤0.07 KB/version stable).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The three-way diff reuses the codec `normalize_outbound` for the compare and
  adds no parallel normalizer; verified by `test_echo_uses_codec_normalize`
  asserting the compare path calls the codec op.
- [ ] Outbound fires only on a rebar-originated change and the baseline stored is
  the value observed after push; verified by `test_echo_observed_after_push` (a
  benign Jira re-canonicalization does not re-sync).
- [ ] A concurrent both-sides edit is detected and flagged under LWW with the
  losing side never silently destroyed; verified by
  `test_concurrent_conflict_detected` (799/799 over the corpus sample).
- [ ] The rich layer stores a change-gated inline 8-byte `rich_sha` and no
  per-pass timestamp, changing 0 entries on a no-op pass; verified by the
  git-delta cost harness reproducing the ≤0.07 KB/version stable profile.
